title: Integer multiplication below n log n
main_claim: A deterministic fixed multitape Turing machine multiplies two n-bit integers in O(n (lg n)^{1-κ}) time, κ=2^{-182}. The two key ingredients are: (1) an address-chunk interchange in O(V u^τ), τ=1-2^{-50}, obtained by recursing through a fixed XOR network whose edge rank sum s_b is less than W_b·m; (2) a simultaneous H0 butterfly layer on D≤d axes in O(V d^{λ'}), built from a fixed Z[i,1/2] network with binary phase frames. Both are plugged into Harvey–van der Hoeven Gaussian resampling, Bluestein chirp and Nussbaumer synthetic transforms.

issues.location: Sec. 7, Lemma no-sort-resampling (eq. gaussian-public-facts, Prop 4.7 norms, Lemmas 4.8-4.12 error/time table)
issues.description: The correctness of the resampling step depends on specific statements from the author-hosted Harvey–van der Hoeven manuscript: the identity T P_s F_s = P_t F_t S under this paper's sign and permutation conventions, the norm bounds ||S'||<3/4 and ||J'||<7/8, and the error/time constants. I could not check these against the source. They are standard, and the hypotheses quoted (gcd(s,t)=1, θ>p/α^4, 2≤α<√p, p>100) match what is checked in Sec. 8. Still, the sign convention for P_t (v_{-sk}) is taken on trust.
issues.evidence: The chirp identity and the cancellation R F^+ R = F^+ were checked by hand: (F^+R_c z)_j=(R_c^{-1}F^+z)_j, and the chirp coefficient exponent is 2πi Σ s j k/t. Neither depends on the HvdH conventions beyond P_s, P_t as defined.

coverage:
I read Sections 0, 2, 3, 4 and 5 in full, Sections 6, 7 and 8 (layout, resampling, chirp, precision, cost table) in substance, and skimmed Sections 9–11. Checks performed:
- All finite-network constants recomputed in python: v, N, I, z_b=13968, z_c=147731, W_b, W_c, s_b, s_c, L/N=100/539 and 101/539, η_b=339/22587335000000, η_c=73/19906842167500, and both η > 20·2^{-50}.
- The scalar network gives y←y+x for arbitrary scratch values in both constructions, from the intersection-coefficient argument.
- Every row of the residual table: label nesting, per-wire sums (data m−1, side m, center m+2h), and the endpoint identities M_sink(ρ(w))−M_source(w)=I, including the 2P_U source edge.
- Frame commutation with pointwise gates, and that Φ_M composes additively.
- The Bruhat-type factorization A=E1ΠE2 and the shear-by-one-interchange trick: (h,d)→(h+d,d) using one interchange.
- The chunk-swap recurrence F_k ≤ (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) and the row-supply argument via high digits.
- The phase-frame algebra with sympy: C=HSH=aI+bX, H0=bSCS, C²=X, C^{-1}=−iZCZ, b²=−i/2. Also weight additivity mod 4 and the 27-coordinate Z correction.
- The 8-step packed parity flip, brute-forced over all integer u,w and c∈{0,1}, plus the guard and bad-fraction bound.
- The complex-layer recurrence and leaf bound.
- The guard-width depth bound (heuristically).
- CRT map Φ, the twist Θ and negacyclic wrap.
- The final error bound 448b·2^{-3b/4}<1/2 and the carry bounds.
- All parameter inequalities and margins with exact rationals: g2=2^{-181}=2κ, g3=2^{-129}, and τ(1+2c)<1−31·2^{-55}<λ.
Not re-derived: the HvdH resampling internals, the Brent-based division corollary, and every fine tape-accounting detail.
sibling_notes: The family 109 board had no prior entries. Note for siblings: the novel content is the network-coding/transparent-computation trick. A rank saving of one per X/Y pair, minus 2h per center wire, is amortized over v=161700 triples, and that yields the sub-linear-in-width chunk interchange. There is no conflict with known lower bounds: Paterson–Fischer–Meyer is for online multiplication only, and the NCC-based Afshani et al. bound is for circuits; TM→circuit simulation loses a log factor.
